caption:
Quinn became an aunty: lots of lifting, rocking and texting baby photos. By day three, the thumb side of the wrist said ouch.

This kind of pain often comes from two thumb tendons getting irritated in a snug tunnel at the wrist. It's common in new parents and heavy phone users. And no, you don't have to stop lifting the baby.

What often helps: a 'scoop' lift with palms under and wrists straight, a thumb-wrist splint on busy days, neutral wrists for feeding and carrying, and giving your thumbs a phone break with voice or two hands. Gradual strengthening comes in as it settles.

If it isn't improving after a proper trial, get it checked and see your GP too.
